item.title: Rick Ross Condo Project Plans 100 More Homes
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Rick Ross' Miami Gardens condo project grew to 770 planned homes as he expanded his stake in the company behind it.
item.content:encoded:
Rick Ross has a bigger plan for the city that raised him, with 100 more homes now part of the condo project he joined this summer.

EnSima Holdings, the real estate company behind the project, said that it now plans 770 homes across 10 floors. The firm aims to finish the work in 2030.

“I partnered with EnSima because I believe in the vision this team is executing right here in my backyard and hometown of Miami Gardens,” said Rick Ross. “Expanding my equity in the group is about the empire we’re continually expanding.”

The firm valued the business at $258 million in its deal with Ross. It also outlined a nonbinding plan for an all-stock sale to an unnamed Nasdaq-listed firm. That sale still needs a final deal and approvals.

Ross first joined the team in July, when AllHipHop covered plans for an eight-story tower near Hard Rock Stadium. The plan included homes and shops. It gave him a role in a new build in his hometown, after years of deals in food, drinks and music.

The first plans for the site were made public in March. By the time Ross signed on, TerraForm Development had been tapped to build it. The team also aimed to open a sales gallery in September to show buyers the range of planned homes.

The sales site still shows the old home count and nine floors. Those figures have yet to catch up with the new plan set out in the release.

The site lists one- and two-bedroom homes at $650 per square foot. Three- and four-bedroom homes are due to come later, with no prices shown. Buyers can choose a building, floor and floor plan on the site to join a waiting list.

The one-bedroom floor plan has 662 square feet. The two-bedroom size is just over a thousand square feet, while the largest planned homes have four bedrooms.

The design puts a pool deck in view of the stadium and pairs homes with shops and green space. Plans call for a roof garden, walking paths and sports courts, plus room for yoga and other classes.

item.title: Usher & Chris Brown Face Refund Petition After Atlanta Concert Falls Short
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Usher and Chris Brown face a refund petition as Atlanta ticket holders demand another shot at the concert they paid for.
item.content:encoded:
Usher and Chris Brown face a refund petition after Atlanta concertgoers paid for a joint show and left feeling shortchanged.

A fan named Rhonda McKenzie wants her November 5 performance at Mercedes-Benz Stadium redone or ticket buyers reimbursed.

Her Change.org petition passed 1,200 signatures by Sunday, adding a formal demand to the complaints about Thursday’s concert. Attendees described a show that began around 10 P.M. despite its advertised 7:30 P.M. start.

McKenzie and other attendees said their tickets cost hundreds of dollars, with some spending thousands expecting both singers to perform together. Instead, they described separate sets without the shared songs that had been part of the tour.

“This is my first concert experience that I went to where I really felt jipped. I really felt I did get robbed,” McKenzie told WSB-TV’s.

Attendees described Chris Brown finishing alone while suspended above the stage, leaving them unsure whether another performance was coming.

The station hadn’t received responses from the singers’ representatives, Live Nation or Ticketmaster, by Sunday night, and neither performer had publicly explained Thursday’s delay.

The petition adds another complaint to a tour that already canceled October stops in Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Columbia. Organizers attributed those cancellations to protecting the health and well-being of the performers and crew during the lengthy stadium run.

Last week’s missing duets also fed rumors that Usher and Chris Brown were feuding, with TMZ reporting an alleged backstage dispute after their separate performances.

Chris Brown pushed back on his Instagram Story with “Internet cap. don’t fall for it,” although he didn’t identify which claim he meant.

They returned to joint performances Friday, including “Back to Sleep” and the “It Depends” remix, before sharing Sunday’s stage too.

Those later appearances followed Thursday’s complaints about the missing collaborations, but the petition seeks a remedy for people who attended the opening Atlanta concert.

The remaining Atlanta concerts are scheduled for November 10 and November 11 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

item.title: Drake Hints He May Retire “Take Care”, But Is Rihanna The Reason?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Drake suggests he may stop performing his Rihanna collaboration “Take Care,” reviving rumors about their romantic history.
item.content:encoded:
Drake is lowkey taking a subliminal shot at ASAP Rocky. Some won’t see it that way. He may be preparing to put one of his most beloved collaborations with Rihanna into permanent retirement. Why bother?

The Toronto superstar recently sang along briefly to “Take Care,” his 2011 collaboration with Rihanna, before suggesting that audiences might not hear him perform the record again.

Now, that is an interesting thing to say about a song that helped define an entire era of his career. Right?

Drake did not explain his remark, leading to the rumors. And whenever Rihanna enters the conversation, we go straight to the past.

Remember, Drake and Rihanna were once one of music’s most fascinating romantic mysteries. We never quite new. Their chemistry produced memorable collaborations, including “What’s My Name?” and “Work.” Was it strictly musical?

Of course, we know their history went beyond the recording studio.

Drake expressed his affection for Rihanna during the 2016 MTV Video Music Awards. That was a 10 years ago, y’all. He was 30. RiRi was not a billionaire yet.

Today, Rihanna has built a family with A$AP Rocky, another major figure in Hip-Hop. Drake has continued navigating his own beefs and rivalries. I won’t say he’s a hater, but he might be a bit jealous of their happy life. Maybe?

Could revisiting “Take Care” simply feel like opening an old chapter that no longer represents where Drake is emotionally?

There is also a less dramatic possibility. Drake might not want to perform the song anymore and that might be the end of it. But this is not a deep cut conversation.

“Take Care” is not an obscure album cut. The record remains one of the defining collaborations of his career.

The Rihanna connection powerful but I think that she curved him back in the day and currently found her man. Drake might be singing the blues because if I had a shot with reonna, I would be singing them right now.

Maybe he is simply tired of singing the song. Maybe it brings back memories. Or maybe he was speaking casually and fans are reading too much into it.

Anyway, let’s play the song and get this over with! We don’t need him to perform it because we can just play it on YouTube like a boss.

item.title: Lil Baby’s FRESH Forecast Low Sales But #1 Is Still Possible
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Baby's FRESH drew a 60,000-plus early forecast, below WHAM's 140,000-unit debut, with the new album's first week still open.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby‘s FRESH has an early chart forecast of 60,000-plus for its first week, giving the rapper a shot at No. 1, though the numbers are well below his last release, WHAM.

FRESH, which came out November 6, still has some time, since the first U.S. tracking week ends November 12, so the full-week count is still to come.

WHAM set a much higher bar last year. It entered the Billboard 200 at No. 1 with 140,000 units from sales and streams. That was its full count for the week ending January 9, 2025. It drew 50,000 from album sales and 90,000 from streams.

The mix of sales and streams is key to reading those totals.

A chart unit can come from an album sale, song sales or streams. Pure sales count copies of the full album bought. Those sales make up just one part of the Billboard 200 count.

WHAM‘s sales push took several forms. Fans could buy it on CD or download it. A version with four extra songs went on sale at his label’s webstore during week one. Fans had to wait until week two to stream those tracks. Both downloads cost $4.99 at the artist and label stores and on iTunes.

His 2022 album It’s Only Me reached No. 1 with an even larger first week of 216,000 units, driven mostly by streams. WHAM then drew a much larger share of its first-week count from full-album sales.

For FRESH, fans had more ways to buy the music before launch. Signed vinyl, CDs and two merch fan packs were offered for pre-order. The digital album has 17 songs. Its release also brought a new video for “Mr. Do Something.”

The album had a hit to build on. “Dead Fresh” first played at a Louis Vuitton show in Paris in June. It later peaked at No. 18 on the Hot 100. The song also reached No. 1 at Urban and Rhythmic radio.

The post didn’t split sales from streams. Its forecast leaves room for FRESH to grow before the week closes and the final chart takes shape.

item.title: Cardi B Challenges BZR’s $2.5M Claim
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Cardi B challenged BZR's payment claims and threatened a countersuit after its chief sought money back for her Jamaica show.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B denied being paid US$2.5 million for her scrapped Jamaica set, while promoter Ryan Burke sought the money back and threatened to sue.

In the video AllHipHop covered last month, she blamed plans that never came together. She said she had kept giving the team time to sort things out, but contracts barred her from sharing the full story. She still wanted to play for her fans in Jamaica.

The BZR WKND chief made his case to CVM News, the Jamaica Observer reported. He said “that money was sent directly to her. She was paid in full.”

He said he sought repayment when a proposed December 20 show looked unlikely and heard nothing back.

Cardi gave her account on Instagram Live Monday evening, November 9: “You sent me a deposit of a million dollars for the show.”

She said the next payment, meant to fund production, never arrived. She also threatened to countersue if BZR took legal action.

Her new payment account tied those stalled plans to the cost of putting on the show.

Cardi had been booked to lead “Cardi B & Friends” at Kingston’s National Stadium on October 18. Her exit left BZR without the star whose name had sold the show for months.

Both sides had taken part in the public launch in August. Cardi’s manager Kelvin Santiago joined promoter Gramps Morgan at AC Hotel Kingston, where the show was pitched as her first in Jamaica and her first stadium date.

When she pulled out in October, Cardi denied that poor ticket sales had caused her exit. Cardi said she had heard more than 18,000 tickets had sold. BZR’s team, meanwhile, asked fans to be patient while it worked through the change.

That earlier statement promised news once the team could confirm more details, without naming a new headliner or laying out a refund plan. Cardi’s team had sent people with ticket questions to the show’s promoters. Her team also told fans to watch her own channels for news of future shows.

Burke now says ticket refunds have started and that all buyers will get their money back.

item.title: How Big Michael Michael Broke Hip-Hop’s Generational Curse
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: Hip-Hop’s generations rarely agree on anything. But Looze Cannon’s “Big Michael Michael” has college kids, OGs and everybody in between dancing to the same beat. Chuck Creekmur explores the culture togetherness.
item.content:encoded:
I decided to hit the Norfolk State vs. Delaware State football game a week or so ago. It was a last-minute decision, made the night before. I had a ball the previous year, the inaugural event. That one was riotous without the riot.

Anyway, I strolled up solo, per usual, and instantly felt at home. I mean, once upon a time, I went to Delaware State and Norfolk State is all too familiar.

Mind you, I am pulling up to the noisy college section. The DJ was playing one of the songs of the year, “Big Michael Michael” by Looze Cannon. And they were ROCKING.

Suddenly, I spotted some of the homies, and they were enjoying themselves, too…in a most age appropriate way. All of this was happening to a song by a dude impersonating Michael Jackson. Now, Michael Jackson impersonators are nothing new. They are all over the place. But this was different.

Looze Cannon, real name Glen Cannon, is an MC who somehow stumbled into this MJ persona through social media. The brother can freestyle, snap on people and create songs on the spot. That’s actually how “Big Michael Michael” came about. He was freestyling on somebody during a livestream, and the moment took on a life of its own.He spotted a play and moved quickly to turn the freestyle into an actual song.

And so it was.

He’s been called a lot of things, from TikTok MJ to Temu Michael Jackson. Other impersonators have even called him a fraud, a disgrace to MJ’s legacy. But somehow, Looze Cannon found a winning formula built on three things: rap skills, comedy skills and an uncanny ability to capture an alternate spirit of the King of Pop.

And let’s be clear. He’s using a filter. He’s not trying to convince anybody he’s actually Michael Jackson. That’s part of the joke. Also, it should be noted that Cannon says AI does nothing to alter or enhance his performance or voice. The visual technology enhances the actual talent. 

His use of social media and business savvy, has him looking like the man of the year.  He initially sold “Big Michael Micheal” directly to fans for $1.99 instead of immediately relying on streaming and it appears that has taken him to the top of the Apple Music charts. At this moment, he’s arguably more culturally impactful than your average rapper with a traditional rollout, a budget and a label behind him. 

Now, let’s consider the genetic makeup of a hit song.

One of the intangibles is the ability to resonate with multiple demographics. And this song seems to be hitting all the markers. We’re talking everybody from 8 to 80. Blind, crippled and crazy, as the old saying goes.

Seriously.

Kids love Big Michael Michael. They think he’s hilarious. College students love him. At the DSU/NSU tailgate, they were all doing selfies and videos to the song simultaneously. The OGs I eventually connected with were discussing how crazy it was that this thing was hitting so hard.

Think about that for a minute.

Hip-Hop has spent years dealing with a generational divide. The old heads don’t understand the young people. The young people don’t care what the old heads think. We argue over lyrics, beats, authenticity, artistry, streaming numbers, who deserves respect and whether the culture has lost its way.

And then here comes a rapper pretending to be Michael Jackson. Kind of, but not really.

Everybody is laughing. Everybody is dancing. Everybody gets it.

And there you have it.

Pressure.

The algorithm has already gotten hold of this virtual King of Pop. In some ways, half his work is done simply by showing up. People recognize Michael Jackson before Looze even opens his mouth. But the recognition alone isn’t what makes this work. Looze has to deliver the goods once he gets their attention.

And he does.

I saw a white dude clipping a piece of the song, and I knew this thing was out of here. It had escaped the usual boundaries. The college kids were on it. The OGs were on it. People who might never agree on a Hip-Hop record were enjoying the same song.

That doesn’t happen every day.

Now, the question is: What next?

Will there be a proper music video? Will he do a remix with Janet or Jermaine? Imagine that. Will he maintain his independence, or will he attempt to scale this into something bigger? Record labels have reportedly been calling, but that doesn’t automatically mean he should sign anything.

And lastly, will he be able to maintain this momentum when he’s just Looze Cannon?

That’s the one I’m really interested in.

He’s got fans, and people genuinely want him to win. But can they follow him beyond the filter? Can he take the audience that came for Michael Jackson and get them invested in Looze Cannon, the artist?

Because eventually, the character and the creator may have to coexist.

In a recent rant aimed at Fabio Jackson, another MJ impersonator and one of his detractors, Looze discussed something that I found particularly interesting. He said his new fans were thanking him. Some found joy in Big Michael Michael. Others said the character helped ease their depression. “I’ve had people tell me that I’m helping them and I’m saving them from what they are going through,” he said on a live out of character. “I’m helping people with their depression, their mental illness.” Still others said the comedy had brought them closer to their children.

That’s bigger than a viral moment.

And that brings me back to Michael Jackson himself.

Despite decades of controversy, accusations and continued attempts by some to tear down his legacy, Michael Jackson remains a force. The movie Michael surpassed $1 billion at the worldwide box office this year. The disconnect between the critics and fans has never been wider, in my view. And now, a funny, talented, Hip-Hop-adjacent impersonator has taken the internet by storm in the most unexpected manner.

Michael Jackson was already a bridge between generations. His music belonged to our parents, to us and, somehow, to our children. Looze Cannon has taken that familiarity and mixed it with modern Hip-Hop, livestream culture, battle-rap instincts and comedy. The result is something that doesn’t require an age bracket.

And that’s why it works.

The old heads recognize Michae and the off-the-dome freestyles as talent. The young people recognize the humor, the memes and the streaming culture. And everybody gets to participate without somebody telling them they’re too old, too young or out of touch. For once, we’re not fighting about what Hip-Hop is supposed to be.

We’re just having fun naturally the way Hip-Hop was intended to be.

So, how does this work going forward?

Only time will tell. For now, this is his year. His literal time.

Somehow, I think his upcoming career could be a Thriller, and people won’t be telling him to “Beat It.”

Or maybe they will. This is the internet, after all. 

But the future doesn’t matter so much right now. Not every cultural moment has to become something else. It can be this. Sometimes, something comes along that everybody can enjoy at the same time.

We’re enjoying ourselves now. That is special and worth celebrating. 

And that’s all there is.

Now.

item.title: Dave Chappelle Faces Backlash As Charlie Kirk Murder Trial Gets Date
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Dave Chappelle's jokes drew criticism as a judge set jury selection for June 2028 in the case over Charlie Kirk's death.
item.content:encoded:
A judge set a trial date for the man charged in Charlie Kirk‘s death as Dave Chappelle‘s jokes about the killing drew harsh words from Kirk’s wife.

Judge Tony Graf ruled on November 9 that the court would begin jury selection on June 21, 2028. Tyler Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and six other charges. The state seeks a death sentence if he is found guilty.

Kirk was shot while he spoke to a crowd at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025. He helped found the right-wing group Turning Point USA.

In September, Judge Graf found grounds to send the case to trial. The judge also ruled that the risk of death to others at the scene let the state seek the death penalty.

The defense team had sought a late 2029 start to give them time to build their case. The state said it could be ready next October. It sought an early date the next year to keep the case out of the year-end holidays. Kirk’s wife wanted it to start by October 4, 2027.

The court acted a day after Kirk’s wife, Erika Kirk, spoke out against comics and pundits who laugh at the deaths of those killed for their views. Her post on X named no one, but came as a clip from Chappelle’s Madison Square Garden show spread online.

“Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but I feel better,” Chappelle said in the clip. He added that “it’s just a feeling.”

Erika called the jokes “beyond disgusting.” She urged people to see the worth of a life even if they do not share that person’s views.

The comic had used Kirk’s death in his stage work before.

As AllHipHop noted, his Netflix special last year turned the death toward his own fear of being shot. He linked early reports about words on the ammo to the anger over his jokes about transgender people.

The judge set aside 105 court days for the case. In April 2028, the court will check whether both sides can finish the work they need to do before they choose a jury.

item.title: Yella Beezy Witness Pressed Over Response Plan After MO3 Killing
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Yella Beezy witness Lynn Scott read texts about a response after MO3 was killed and faced questions about what she knew.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy‘s first defense witness read texts about plans for his response on the day MO3 was killed. A prosecutor pressed her on why she felt he needed one.

Lynn Scott, who worked in marketing at his label Hitco in 2020, took the stand in Dallas on November 9. Court reporter Meghann Cuniff posted footage of the hearing, where Scott faced questions about her texts after the shooting.

Yella Beezy, born Markies Conway, pleaded not guilty to capital murder and denied a role in MO3’s death. Prosecutors accused him of paying Kewon White to kill the rapper, born Melvin Noble.

Scott said she was in California with Yella Beezy on November 11, 2020, the day MO3 was killed on Interstate 35E in Dallas. Asked if she could recall texts about a response that day, she said, “No, I don’t remember.”

The prosecutor showed her a group text from Yella Beezy’s iCloud account. Scott said the phone number was hers and agreed that she had sent the texts. She read a text sent that afternoon: “We need to hop on a call to strategize messaging around what just happened in Dallas.”

She read a second text: “We need to have him craft a response.”

Asked if police had been in touch with her by then about any role Yella Beezy had in the killing, she said no. She also said he had not spoken to her that day about hiring White to kill MO3.

Pressed on the need for a response plan, Scott said she thought they should be prepared.

The state had rested its case before Scott took the stand. Judge Chika Anyiam denied the defense’s request to dismiss the charge for lack of evidence.

Earlier in the trial, Jose Bodega, Yella Beezy’s childhood friend, recanted his grand jury account. On November 2, he told jurors he made up his claim that the rapper wanted MO3 dead.

Judge Anyiam let jurors use the earlier account to weigh whether Bodega had told the truth. It could not serve as proof that the claimed plot took place.

White was found guilty in his own trial on September 4, 2026 and sentenced to life without parole.

item.title: Charlamagne Rejects Violence After Chappelle's Kirk Joke
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Charlamagne Tha God objected to violence over opinions as "The Breakfast Club" discussed Dave Chappelle's Charlie Kirk joke.
item.content:encoded:
Radio host Charlamagne Tha God pushed back on Dave Chappelle‘s joke about feeling better since Charlie Kirk‘s death, saying he did not want people shot for what they think.

His response came Monday, November 9, after the show played a short clip from the comedian’s set at Madison Square Garden in New York.

“Any of us can be shot. And I don’t want anybody getting shot because somebody disagrees with their opinion,” he said.

He stressed that “you have the freedom” to joke about any topic, but said he did not want to deal with that energy in his own life. He would not wish such a death on his worst enemy.

The panel also asked if there was more to the joke than the video showed, and there was. Chappelle’s joke was a sly play on Tony Hinchcliffe’s joke about George Floyd during “The Roast of Kevin Hart” on Netflix.

Chappelle played the Garden on November 6 and 7. At his request, the ban barred cameras, smart glasses and phones.

The rules required small devices to stay in locked Yondr pouches, which fans kept with them throughout the show.

But footage leaked showing Chappelle talking about Kirk’s killing and relating it to his own fears as a public speaker before the Garden shows.

“It’s scary being a public speaker. Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but I feel better,” Chappelle said.

The comedian added: “I’m sure Charlie Kirk is looking up at us right now, laughing so hard he can’t breathe,” a play on Hinchcliff’s controversial George Floyd joke.

Kirk was shot and killed while speaking at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025. He was 31.

Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk, had posted her own statement on X on November 8. She spoke out against leftist comics, podcasters and pundits who made light of political killings.

She did not name Chappelle. She urged people to see the value of a life even when they do not share that person’s views. She also warned that laughing at such deaths would harm the country’s shared values.

item.title: Ice Cube’s BIG3 Swaps NFTs For League Equity To Ambassador To Denmark
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ice Cube's BIG3 exchanged Ken Howery's team-linked NFTs for league equity while pursuing a planned stock-market merger.
item.content:encoded:
Ice Cube‘s BIG3 three-on-three basketball league exchanged PayPal co-founder Ken Howery’s Fire-tier NFTs for equity under a settlement newly detailed by The Washington Sun.

Howery, who also serves as U.S. Ambassador to Denmark under the Trump administration, joined the rollout alongside Snoop Dogg.

In May 2022, the league announced that the two had teamed up to purchase all 25 Fire-tier tokens tied to the team Big3 team, Bivouac.

The report placed his NFT holdings between $100,001 and $250,000. It did not value the BIG3 HoldCo LLC units he received.

The broader buyer dispute moved into individual arbitration after purchasers accused BIG3 of “deceptive, fraudulent, and illegal marketing” over team-sale benefits. They alleged the league renamed sold teams while calling the originals “on hiatus.”

BIG3 disputed the allegations.

BIG3’s original 2022 package mixed fan access with a say in team decisions. Each franchise was allotted 25 Fire-tier tokens and 975 Gold-tier tokens, giving the offer a team-by-team structure.

Fire-tier tokens were offered at $25,000 each, compared with $5,000 for Gold-tier tokens.

Buyers were promised game access and votes on team representatives, uniform colors and league awards. Fire holders were also offered the right to use their team’s name and logo to make and sell artwork and designs.

The financial benefits came with conditions. Fire-tier holders were promised a collective 40 percent of net proceeds from a future team sale, subject to regulatory approval. Separately, the package offered an opportunity to obtain shares at the initial public offering price if BIG3 went public.

The Sun also cited an October disclosure that BIG3 had “entered into settlement agreements with two NFT purchasers” in 2025, followed by two more in the first half of 2026.

In June, BIG3 and Graf Global announced plans to merge, creating a path from holding-company equity to public stock.

The terms called for existing equity and equity-linked holdings to convert into shares of the combined company at closing.

The June agreement valued BIG3 at $290 million before new funding and potential earnouts. Its closing conditions included shareholder and regulatory approvals, a stock-exchange listing and at least $50 million in net cash proceeds. Howery’s units would become public-company stock only if the merger closes.
